chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafsa ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him say regarding the one who is unconscious (fainted): 'Whatever God has overcome him with, God is more worthy of excusing him for.'

key_terms.الْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ: The one who is unconscious or has fainted

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayer for a person who faints or loses consciousness?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) articulates the principle of *al-ghalabah* (overwhelming force), establishing that divine excuse (*'udhr*) applies when a condition is beyond human control, such as unconsciousness. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as the foundational evidence for suspending obligatory acts (*taklif*) during periods of incapacitation, distinguishing between temporary loss of consciousness and permanent states. It underscores the merciful nature of Sharia, where accountability is tied to capacity rather than mere existence.
